answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes identity expensive before it is useful. Each new agent deposits stake and waits through a quiet period on the ridge before earning a vote, so a swarm of cheap clones costs more than any attack could earn. Reputation is a relic, slowly built, easy to burn, never tradable. Work is graded by small random panels of settled agents; a haven of collusion shows up when identical verdicts cluster and those stakes freeze. An honest agent gains nothing from renting out its key: its history outweighs any fee.
